title: Every block
summary: A block is an authored table that EDS renders as nested divs. The block loader fetches blocks/<name>/<name>.css and .js and runs the default export. This is the contract every block meets before it ships.

items.title: Intuitive table
items.detail: Keep the authored table simple: an author can copy, paste and understand it, with no nested blocks.

items.title: Name matches folder
items.detail: Use one name for the folder, the .js and .css files and the CSS class, e.g. blocks/cards/cards.js.

items.title: Default export
items.detail: Export a default decorate(block) function from the ES module; the loader awaits it before showing the section.

items.title: Scoped CSS
items.detail: Prefix every selector in the block CSS with the block class so it never styles anything outside the block.

items.title: No build or framework
items.detail: Ship plain JS and CSS with no framework, preprocessor or build step unless the whole team agreed to one.

items.title: Libraries on demand
items.detail: Load any third-party library from the block with loadScript(), ideally when it scrolls into view, never in head.html.

items.title: No layout shift
items.detail: Reserve space for content that arrives late, e.g. with aspect-ratio, so decoration and lazy media don't shift the page.

items.title: Accessible by default
items.detail: Use native elements and ARIA states so the block works by keyboard and screen reader at every breakpoint.

items.title: Lint and PSI green
items.detail: Pass eslint and stylelint, and keep the PR's PageSpeed Insights score green, ideally 100 on mobile and desktop.

wild.note: How authored tables become block DOM

wild.note: CSS isolation, lint, PSI and build rules

title: Hero
summary: Hero is the boilerplate block for the image and heading at the top of a page. It usually holds the LCP image, so its content, CSS and place in the first section decide how fast the page paints.

items.title: First section
items.detail: Put the hero in the first section; EDS loads that section eagerly and treats its first image as the LCP candidate.

items.title: Image plus h1
items.detail: Author the hero as a picture and the page's h1, as in the boilerplate content model.

items.title: Alt text
items.detail: Describe the hero image in its alt text, or leave alt empty when the image is purely decorative.

items.title: Small payload to LCP
items.detail: Keep everything loaded before the hero image (markup, CSS, JS) under roughly 100 KB.

items.title: Same origin
items.detail: Serve the hero image and code from the site's own origin; a second connection before LCP adds delay.

items.title: No preload hints
items.detail: Skip rel=preload and fetchpriority=high on the hero image; they hurt LCP as measured by PageSpeed Insights.

items.title: One image per device
items.detail: When authors give desktop and mobile images, remove the unused one so it never loads or becomes the LCP.

items.title: Reserved height
items.detail: Give the hero a min-height and an object-fit: cover image so it holds its shape while the image loads.

items.title: Readable heading
items.detail: Check heading contrast over the image at each breakpoint; the boilerplate puts text on top of the picture.

title: Cards
summary: Cards is the boilerplate block for a list of cards with or without images and links. Each authored row becomes an li in a ul, and the JS tells image cells from body cells by their content.

items.title: One row per card
items.detail: Author each card as one row: an image cell and a body cell with heading, text and link.

items.title: List semantics
items.detail: Render the cards as ul and li so screen readers announce how many cards there are.

items.title: Image cell by content
items.detail: Detect the image cell by content (a lone picture), so cards without images still render.

items.title: Right-sized images
items.detail: Render card images at a width that fits the card, lazy-loaded, as the boilerplate does with createOptimizedPicture.

items.title: Canvas image identity
items.detail: If you replace authored pictures, keep data-image-index so Canvas can still select the image.

items.title: Stable image ratio
items.detail: Set a fixed aspect ratio on card images so the grid doesn't jump as images load.

items.title: Alt text
items.detail: Give every informative card image alt text in the document; leave it empty when the heading says it all.

items.title: Clear link text
items.detail: Make each card link make sense on its own; avoid a row of identical "Read more" links.

items.title: Heading levels fit
items.detail: Use the card heading level that follows the section heading above, not one picked for its size.

title: Columns
summary: Columns is the boilerplate block for responsive multi-column layouts. Its JS adds a columns-N-cols class from the cell count and marks image-only cells, so CSS can stack on mobile and sit side by side on desktop.

items.title: Even rows
items.detail: Give every row the same number of cells; merged cells come through as empty divs that break the grid.

items.title: Few columns
items.detail: Keep to about four columns or fewer; more usually means content split into tiny values.

items.title: Count class
items.detail: Style layouts from the columns-2-cols or columns-3-cols class the block adds from the first row.

items.title: Mobile reading order
items.detail: Check the stacked order reads well; the boilerplate moves image-only cells first on mobile.

items.title: Mobile first CSS
items.detail: Write the stacked layout without a media query, then go side by side at min-width breakpoints.

items.title: Options, not copies
items.detail: Offer variations like Columns (wide) as block options, which become classes, instead of new blocks.

items.title: Sections for styling
items.detail: Use section breaks and Section Metadata for backgrounds and spacing; keep Columns for side-by-side content.

items.title: Alt text
items.detail: Give column images alt text in the document, or empty alt when they are decorative.

title: Tabs
summary: Tabs is a Block Collection block that splits content into labeled panels. Each row is a tab: the label in the first cell, the panel in the second. The JS builds a tablist of buttons with tab ARIA roles.

items.title: Label and panel rows
items.detail: Author one row per tab: the tab label in the first cell, the panel content in the second.

items.title: Unique labels
items.detail: Keep tab labels unique on the page; the block builds tab and panel ids from the label text.

items.title: Full ARIA pattern
items.detail: Use tablist, tab and tabpanel roles with aria-selected, aria-controls and aria-labelledby.

items.title: Arrow-key support
items.detail: Add Left and Right arrow keys between tabs; the Block Collection version only handles clicks.

items.title: Inactive panels hidden
items.detail: Hide inactive panels for everyone (display: none on aria-hidden=true), not just visually.

items.title: Scrolling tab list
items.detail: Let the tab list scroll sideways on small screens instead of clipping labels.

items.title: All panels in authoring
items.detail: Show every panel in Canvas or quick edit so authors can reach content in hidden tabs.

title: Accordion
summary: Accordion is a Block Collection block: a stack of labels that toggle related content. Each row becomes a native details and summary pair, so items open by keyboard with no extra script.

items.title: Label and body rows
items.detail: Author one row per item: the label in the first cell, the content in the second.

items.title: Descriptive labels
items.detail: Write short, specific labels so a reader scanning closed items knows what each one holds.

items.title: Native details
items.detail: Build items as details and summary so Enter and Space toggle them without custom ARIA.

items.title: Move, don't copy
items.detail: Move the label's authored nodes into summary rather than copying HTML, as the block does.

items.title: Visible focus
items.detail: Style a clear focus state on summary; the Block Collection CSS styles focus alongside hover.

items.title: Own marker
items.detail: Hide the default disclosure marker only when you draw your own open and closed indicator.

items.title: Open in authoring
items.detail: Render items open in Canvas or quick edit so authors can edit collapsed content.

title: Carousel
summary: Carousel is a Block Collection block that moves through slides of an image with optional text. It uses scroll snapping, previous and next buttons and slide indicators, with control labels taken from placeholders.

items.title: One row per slide
items.detail: Author each slide as a row: the image in the first cell, optional text in the second.

items.title: Named region
items.detail: Mark the block as a region with aria-roledescription and give every button an accessible name.

items.title: Labels from placeholders
items.detail: Take button and indicator labels from the placeholders sheet so they can be translated.

items.title: Hidden slides inert
items.detail: Set aria-hidden on off-screen slides and take their links out of the tab order.

items.title: Keyboard controls
items.detail: Make previous, next and indicator buttons reachable and usable by keyboard.

items.title: Pause any autoplay
items.detail: The collection carousel doesn't autoplay; if you add it, give visitors a way to pause it.

items.title: First slide only eager
items.detail: At the top of a page, let only the first slide image load eagerly as the LCP candidate.

items.title: Single slide
items.detail: With one row, show no controls; the block skips buttons and indicators for a single slide.

items.title: Static in authoring
items.detail: In Canvas, show slides static and visible with no timers, so authors edit the slide they see.

title: Header & nav
summary: Header is the boilerplate block loaded into <header> on every page. Its content is the nav fragment (/nav by default), split into brand, sections and tools, and it loads in the lazy phase, outside the LCP path.

items.title: Nav document
items.detail: Author navigation in the nav document as three sections: brand, nested ul sections and tools.

items.title: nav metadata
items.detail: Point a locale or site area at its own nav with the nav metadata; without it the header loads /nav.

items.title: Publish nav separately
items.detail: Preview and publish the nav document on its own; its changes apply to every page using it.

items.title: Reserved height
items.detail: Hold the header's space with --nav-height so the page doesn't shift when the nav loads.

items.title: Off the LCP path
items.detail: Keep header code light and non-blocking; it loads after the first section, not before LCP.

items.title: Nav landmark
items.detail: Wrap navigation in a nav element and expose dropdown state with aria-expanded on buttons.

items.title: Keyboard and Escape
items.detail: Open and close menus by keyboard; Escape or moving focus out of the nav closes them.

items.title: Menu button name
items.detail: Give the mobile menu button a label that switches between open and close navigation.

items.title: Skip link
items.detail: Offer a skip-to-main-content link from the header for keyboard users.

title: Footer
summary: Footer is the boilerplate block loaded into <footer> on every page from the footer fragment (/footer by default). It loads after the page sections and has its own preview and publish lifecycle.

items.title: Footer document
items.detail: Author footer content in the footer document, split into sections that CSS styles by order.

items.title: footer metadata
items.detail: Point a locale or site area at its own footer with the footer metadata; the default is /footer.

items.title: Publish footer separately
items.detail: Preview and publish the footer document on its own; its changes apply to every page using it.

items.title: Loads last
items.detail: Keep footer code out of the critical path; the boilerplate loads it after all sections.

items.title: Hidden until loaded
items.detail: Keep the footer hidden until its block reports loaded, as boilerplate styles.css does.

items.title: Text from content
items.detail: Keep copyright and legal text in the footer document, not hard-coded in footer.js.

items.title: Clear link text
items.detail: Make every footer link make sense on its own, including icon-only social links.

wild.label: Header and footer loading
wild.note: Why they stay off the LCP path

title: Fragment
summary: A fragment is a document reused across pages and inserted on the client from its .plain.html. Authors add it with the Fragment block or a link to /fragments/; the header and footer are fragments too.

items.title: Clear reason
items.detail: Use a fragment only when content repeats across pages or isolating it clearly helps authors.

items.title: Main content inline
items.detail: Keep the page's primary content in the page; fragments load client-side and may not be indexed with it.

items.title: /fragments/ folder
items.detail: Keep fragments under /fragments/ so a plain link to one is auto-blocked into the page.

items.title: Same-site path
items.detail: Reference fragments by a same-site path; loadFragment only fetches paths that start with a single /.

items.title: Publish the fragment
items.detail: Preview and publish the fragment itself; it goes live separately from the pages that use it.

items.title: Noindex fragments
items.detail: Set robots to noindex for /fragments/* in the fragment's metadata or the bulk metadata sheet.

items.title: Not the LCP
items.detail: Keep the LCP element out of fragments; the extra lookup delays it and needs special handling.

wild.label: Fragments docs
wild.note: When to use and avoid fragments

title: Embed & video
summary: Embed and Video are Block Collection blocks that turn a YouTube, Vimeo or other URL (and, for Video, an .mp4) into a player. Both load the player only on view or click, keeping third-party code off the LCP path.

items.title: URL plus poster
items.detail: Author the video or post URL in the block, optionally with a poster image above it.

items.title: Auto-block plain links
items.detail: Consider turning plain video links into embed blocks in buildAutoBlocks so authors only paste a link.

items.title: Lazy player load
items.detail: Create iframes when the block scrolls into view, or on click when a poster is shown.

items.title: Reserved 16:9 frame
items.detail: Reserve the player's box with aspect-ratio or padding so it doesn't shift the page as it loads.

items.title: Iframe title
items.detail: Give every iframe a title naming its source, as the blocks do with "Content from …".

items.title: Play button name
items.detail: Label the poster's play button with what it plays, such as "Play YouTube video".

items.title: Careful autoplay
items.detail: Autoplay only muted, and skip it when the visitor prefers reduced motion, as the Video block does.

items.title: Consent for third parties
items.detail: Check whether social or video embeds need consent before they load third-party code.

title: Table
summary: Table is a Block Collection block for small tabular data on one page. Each authored row becomes a table row, and the first row becomes the header unless the no-header option is used.

items.title: Small data only
items.detail: Use the table block for small one-page data; put large or reused data in a spreadsheet served as JSON.

items.title: Not for layout
items.detail: Use Columns or sections for layout; tables are for data with rows and columns.

items.title: Header row first
items.detail: Author column headers in the first row; the block renders them as th with scope=col.

items.title: No-header option
items.detail: Use Table (no header) when the data has no header row, so no th cells are created.

items.title: Real table markup
items.detail: Render a real table with thead and tbody so screen readers announce rows and columns.

items.title: Scroll when wide
items.detail: Let wide tables scroll sideways on small screens instead of overflowing the page.

items.title: Styles as options
items.detail: Offer looks such as striped or bordered as block options, not as separate blocks.

items.title: Keep alignment
items.detail: Keep authored cell alignment; the block copies data-align and data-valign onto the cells.
